metadata.scenario: Full one-week (168-hour) OPSD/CoSSMic replay, identical starting network and input for all three modes. No faults injected -- the stress in this window is the recorded academic demand peak at hour 48 (2016-06-08 06:00 UTC), which coincides with near-zero EV load and low solar, pushing feeder F2 to ~137% loading under no intervention. See section 20 (Experimental Evaluation) in README.md.

dataset.source: Open Power System Data, Household Data v2020-04-15 (CoSSMic, Konstanz, Germany)

labels.RECORDED: Academic, EV, facility and solar profiles (OPSD/CoSSMic, scaled to campus peaks)
labels.SIMULATED: Hospital demand (fixed 380kW), battery capacity/SOC/reserve, network topology, electrical parameters, and (mode B) the load-shedding rule / (mode C) the flexibility market's offer costs and policies
labels.DERIVED: Feeder/transformer loading percent and bus voltages -- pandapower AC power-flow output, not asserted numbers
labels.MEASURED: Every number in `summary` below, computed by actually executing each strategy over the identical 168-hour input -- not fabricated or hand-tuned per mode

modes.no_intervention: The grid follows the recorded/assumed input with no corrective action.
modes.load_shedding: Deterministic rule: shed 10% of each overloaded feeder's non-hospital load per iteration until resolved or a 30-iteration cap is hit. Hospital is never a shedding candidate. No market, no battery dispatch.
modes.market_system: Rust agent_engines binary (offers + clear_market + settle) + Python AC power-flow validation (grid_engine.scenarios), with settled actions applied to the running network -- the same pipeline the live demo uses.
